source.dataset: NASA/SPDF OMNIweb High Resolution OMNI (HRO), 5-min resolution
source.expected_lines_full_year_5min: 365 days * 288 samples/day = 105120 (1989 is not a leap year) -- matches exactly

column_used.description: Whitespace-delimited ASCII, 49 fields per line, no header row. Field order confirmed against hroformat.txt (common HRO block: Year I4, Day I4, Hour I3, Minute I3, spacecraft IDs, IMF/plasma parameters, spacecraft position, then 'Ancillary Data' block AE, AL, AU, SYM/D, SYM/H, ASY/D, ASY/H, PC(N), Magnetosonic Mach number, then (5-min only) 3 GOES proton flux fields appended at the end -> 49 fields total, matching the observed field count).
column_used.verification: First data row's ancillary block reproduces the documented order exactly: field41=-1 (SYM/D, real value even though AE/AL/AU at fields 38-40 are fill=99999), field42=-39 (SYM/H), field43=64 (ASY/D), field44=35 (ASY/H), field45=2.96 (PC(N)), field46=99.9 (Magnetosonic Mach fill). Global minimum of field42 across the full 1989 file is -714 nT, occurring at day=73 (=1989-03-14), hour=0, minutes 40-50 UT -- matches the independently-known 'Quebec Blackout' storm SYM-H minimum of -714 nT cited in PHASE0_5_SURVEY_NEW_CANDIDATES.md, confirming the column identification.

fill_value_handling.note: SYM/H (unlike AE/AL/AU, which do have many fill=99999 rows in this file since they need more magnetometer stations) has ZERO fill values anywhere in the 1989 file. No interpolation, gap-filling, or exclusion was needed for the segments actually used; the check was performed explicitly (equality to 99999) rather than assumed.

ssc_primary.source: Boteler 2019, Space Weather 17:1427 (documented externally, provided in task instructions)
ssc_primary.boundary_rule: A 5-min HRO record's (hour, minute) label is the START of its averaging interval (per hroformat.txt). Boundary rule applied: a record belongs to PRE if (day < 72) or (day==72 and hour*60+minute < 87); it belongs to POST (until the next transition) if (day>72 or (day==72 and hour*60+minute>=87)) and before the POST-segment upper bound below. This assigns the record labeled 1989-03-13 01:25 (85 min-of-day < 87) to PRE and the record labeled 01:30 (90 >= 87) to POST -- the first POST record already shows the SSC signature (SYM/H jumps from 29 nT at 01:25 to 68 nT at 01:30).

post_upper_bound.chosen_rule: next documented storm event visible directly in the data (not a fixed calendar window)
post_upper_bound.rationale: Daily min/max SYM/H in the recovery tail of the March-13 storm gradually approaches quiet levels by ~day 83-85 (daily min rises from -714 on day73 to -11 on day85). At 1989-03-26 22:45-22:55 UT (day 85), SYM/H jumps abruptly from 9 nT to 36 nT then 50-65 nT -- a second, distinct SSC-like sudden commencement signature, i.e. the onset of a new storm, found directly by inspecting the downloaded data rather than assumed a priori. POST (primary) is therefore bounded at this second transition using the same boundary rule as SSC1 (record label < day85 22:50 UT is the last POST record; the record at day85 22:50 UT, where the jump is already visible, and everything after it, is excluded as belonging to the NEXT storm, a documented confounder external to the March-13 event).
post_upper_bound.deviation_note: METHODOLOGY_NOTE.md gap (d) allows either 'until the next documented storm event, if any' or 'a fixed reasonable recovery period, explicitly documented' -- this run uses the former, with the 'next event' identified empirically in the downloaded SYM/H series itself (a second SSC-like jump) rather than from an external storm catalog citation. This is disclosed explicitly as the chosen convention, not asserted as an externally pre-documented event time.

pre_primary.rule: All continuous available SYM/H in the downloaded 1989 record strictly before the SSC boundary (day<72, or day==72 and minute-of-day<87).

pre_robust.rule: Most recent 50% of pre_primary BY SAMPLE COUNT (last floor(20466/2)=10233 samples, i.e. samples[10233:]).

post_primary.rule: All continuous available SYM/H from the SSC boundary (inclusive) up to (exclusive of) the next documented/observed storm transition.

post_robust.rule: Closest-to-transition 50% of post_primary BY SAMPLE COUNT (first floor(4000/2)=2000 samples, i.e. samples[:2000]).

pipeline_provenance.module: 05_DISCOVERY_LAB/02_TESTS/TRI_RG/mse_multiscale_entropy/analysis/mse_common.py (UNMODIFIED -- called via run_mse_pipeline only, per task instructions)
pipeline_provenance.no_decimation: No decimation or resampling of the SYM/H series was performed -- all 4 segments (20466, 10233, 4000, 2000 samples) ran the full pipeline (200 IAAFT surrogates x 50 iterations each) directly, well within tractable runtime (see wall_clock_seconds below).

runtime.note: Both runs executed synchronously in the foreground (no backgrounding of the pipeline calculation itself), per task instructions.
